title: test(plugin-auth): fail the D7 collision guard on unmapped better-auth-managed objects
body:
Fixes #7770

## What was wrong

`managed-extension-fields.test.ts` derives better-auth's owned column surface through `MODEL_TO_OBJECT`, and the collision loop skipped anything that map did not produce:

```ts
const owned = byObject[object];
if (!owned) continue;
```

So an object declaring `managedBy: 'better-auth'` but absent from the map got **zero** collision coverage while reading as covered from the outside. `sys_api_key` has been in exactly that position since #7727 gave it its first `MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS` entry. Nine objects were mapped; 22 declare `managedBy: 'better-auth'`.

## What it does now

Closes the class rather than the instance, on the `SINGLE_RECORD_WRITE_ONLY` pattern from `packages/spec/src/data/api-methods-batch-conformance.test.ts` — register the exception with the reason, and fail on a stale registration.

The diff is pure insertion (325 added, 0 removed): every existing assertion survives byte-for-byte, five are added around them.

1. **Scan, not a hand list.** Every `*.object.ts` under `packages/` is scanned for a line-anchored `managedBy: 'better-auth'` (the anchor keeps a prose mention in a comment from reading as a declaration). Same reasoning as the exemplar: an audit whose scope is a package name misses the declaration that lands in a package nobody thought to open. A floor assertion guards a silently empty sweep.
2. **Mapped or registered.** Every scanned object is in `MODEL_TO_OBJECT` or in the new `UNMAPPED_MANAGED_OBJECTS` registry with a reason. Thirteen entries today: `sys_api_key`, three opt-in core plugins this file does not load, sso/scim (which expose no `schema` option for `getAuthTables()` to read, #3653), and the seven `@better-auth/oauth-provider` objects that have their own gate.
3. **Nothing declared is silently skipped.** An unmapped object may carry `MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS` entries only when its registry entry claims `noBetterAuthColumns` — better-auth owns no column on that table at all. `sys_api_key` is the only such entry, and the only unmapped object with declared fields. The positive half is pinned too: the objects actually compared are asserted to be exactly `sys_invitation`, `sys_organization`, `sys_user`.
4. **Staleness.** A registry entry that is no longer a declared managed object, or that is now mapped, fails as stale — an exemption that documents nothing is the failure mode the exemption was meant to prevent.
5. **Coverage cannot shrink.** The nine covered objects are pinned as a literal, and both `MODEL_TO_OBJECT` and the derived surface are asserted against it.

## The obvious fix is refused, in the failure text

Adding `apikey: 'sys_api_key'` to the map would compare better-auth's apiKey surface against `MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS[sys_api_key]`, which lists `revoked` and nothing else — a green check over a table with essentially no coverage, the same defect surviving its own fix. Completing that list is not a free move either: the same map is the ADR-0092 D2 write whitelist, so adding `name` / `prefix` / `key` / `user_id` / `expires_at` widens what a generic write surface may touch on a credential table. That is a security change and this PR does not make it.

Both failure messages say so, because the failure message is the deliverable for whoever hits it. Verbatim from the run:

```
these objects declare managedBy: 'better-auth' but are absent from MODEL_TO_OBJECT, so
this guard skips them entirely and any extension field declared on them gets ZERO
collision coverage while reading as covered: sys_api_key
(packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key.object.ts). Pick one deliberately:
  (a) MAP IT — and it takes both halves, in this order: 1. pass the plugin that owns the
model into the getAuthTables() call in betterAuthFieldsByObject(), because a map entry
alone derives no table and the object stays silently skipped; 2. add the
model: 'object_name' entry to MODEL_TO_OBJECT.
  (b) REGISTER IT in UNMAPPED_MANAGED_OBJECTS with the reason better-auth owns no
derivable surface for it here.
  Do NOT complete MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS just to make the comparison look meaningful:
that map is also the ADR-0092 D2 write whitelist, so adding a column there widens what a
generic write surface may touch. On a credential table that is a security change, not a
test fix. Coverage of the columns better-auth itself owns is the parity gate's job
(better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts), not D7's.
```

Note step 1 is the third trap from the issue thread, stated first: a map entry alone derives no table and the object stays skipped.

## One correction to the issue's premise

The issue anticipates the day better-auth's `apiKey` plugin is enabled. **There is no such plugin at the pinned version.** better-auth 1.7.0-rc.2 publishes no `better-auth/plugins/api-key` subpath, and `better-auth/plugins` exports no `apiKey` — the columns the issue lists belong to a plugin that is not in the dependency graph at all.

That does not weaken the card; it strengthens the exemption and gives it a sharper tripwire. A dedicated test pins the premise, so the exemption expires at the **dependency bump** rather than waiting for an enablement decision — one step earlier than the card anticipated. Its message names the reconciliation as an ownership decision and explicitly rules out widening `MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS` to reach it.

## Verification

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test` — 40 files, 1003 tests, all green. `typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean on the changed file, `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` OK. Built the dependency closure first (`--filter '@objectstack/plugin-auth^...' build`).

Five ablations, each with the direction predicted before running:

| mutation | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|
| A — remove the `sys_api_key` exemption | red on 2, collision test stays green | as predicted, plus a third red: the mutation renamed the key rather than deleting it, so staleness fired too |
| B — keep the entry, drop `noBetterAuthColumns` | red on "silently skipped" only | as predicted |
| C — exempt `sys_user`, an object that is mapped | red on staleness | as predicted |
| D — point the premise tripwire at a symbol that exists | red, with the re-decide message | as predicted |
| E — delete `teamMember: 'sys_team_member'` | red on the coverage pin and on accounting | **inverted** — see below |

The collision assertion staying **green** through ablation A is the point: that green, alone, is precisely what #7770 reports.

Ablation E is the one worth reading. The prediction was wrong, and it was wrong because the assertion was: the coverage pin compared the derived surface against `Object.values(MODEL_TO_OBJECT)`, both sides moving with the same map, so deleting a mapping shrank expectation and reality together and the pin stayed green. Fixed in the second commit by writing the nine objects out as a literal; re-run after the fix produced the two reds originally predicted.

## Reporting duties from the dispatch (analysis, no changes)

**Does `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts` share the blind spot?** Not the same one. It iterates the *derived model set*, so an object missing from its `PLATFORM_OBJECTS` map cannot be silently skipped — the day `apiKey()` entered its plugin list, its "every better-auth model maps to a platform object" assertion would fail loudly with `apikey → apikey`. Today it derives no apikey model and asserts nothing about `sys_api_key`, which is correct: better-auth writes no column there. What both gates *do* share is the upstream precondition — each hand-maintains its own plugin list and nothing reconciles either against `auth-manager.ts`'s actual assembly. Enabling a plugin in the auth manager while forgetting the test's list leaves both gates silent. Reported, not fixed.

**What happens the day the apiKey plugin is enabled?** The premise test goes red first, at the bump that makes the plugin available, before anyone can enable it. Its message names the fork (keep the hand-rolled table, or adopt the plugin) and, for the adopt branch, all four steps: map `apikey`, pass `apiKey()` to `getAuthTables()` here, add `sys_api_key` to the parity gate, and reconcile `name` / `prefix` / `key` / `user_id` / `expires_at` as an ownership decision rather than by widening the D2 whitelist. If instead someone maps the object without the premise expiring, the staleness assertion fails and names the entry to drop.

## Out of scope, filed

**#7820** — the second axis of the same blindness, found while verifying this one. This file's `getAuthTables()` loads `organization` only, while the auth manager loads many more behind flags, so a column an unloaded plugin owns is invisible even for a **mapped** object. `sys_user.phone_number` is a live instance: it is declared in `MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS.sys_user` and it is the column better-auth's `phoneNumber` plugin writes (mapped explicitly by `AUTH_PHONE_NUMBER_USER_FIELDS`). Deliberately not fixed here — widening the plugin set turns this guard red on an ownership question nobody has decided. It is the only overlap; I checked every other declared extension field against the wider surface.

## Changeset

None — `skip-changeset`. The diff is one `.test.ts` file. No shipped code, no published artifact, nothing user-visible.
